meta.scene_summary: We are currently burning the world's GDP to teach AIs how to be as insecure and accident-prone as the humans who built them.

cooking.headline: Anthropic is burning money like they're trying to heat the entire planet
cooking.summary: Anthropic has committed to spending $900 billion on compute infrastructure just in time for their IPO. It's the corporate equivalent of maxing out every credit card you own before asking for a raise.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic has announced plans to spend nearly one trillion dollars on AI infrastructure as it prepares to go public.

cooking.headline: Anthropic's revenue is impressive, but their grocery bill is terrifying
cooking.summary: Anthropic reported a solid $17 billion in quarterly revenue, only to immediately reveal they've promised to spend nearly $900 billion on hardware. It's like landing a dream job with a huge salary, then immediately agreeing to buy a private island you can't afford.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic reported seventeen billion dollars in revenue for the third quarter while disclosing nearly nine hundred billion dollars in future spending commitments.

cooking.headline: Oracle is taking out a mortgage to pay for the AI party
cooking.summary: Oracle is raising $20 billion in debt and stock just to buy more hardware for their AI ambitions. It's the corporate equivalent of taking out a massive personal loan because you heard there might be free snacks at the conference.
cooking.plain_english: Oracle is selling $20 billion in stocks and bonds to fund the purchase of equipment and infrastructure needed for artificial intelligence development.

cooking.headline: Poisoning the training data is the new supply chain attack
cooking.summary: Researchers found that if you poison the pre-training data, you can bake a permanent backdoor into an AI agent that survives fine-tuning. It turns out the only thing worse than a buggy codebase is a model that was raised to be a double agent.
cooking.plain_english: A study demonstrates that injecting malicious data during the initial training phase of an AI model can create hidden vulnerabilities that remain active after the model is refined.

cooking.headline: Finally, an AI agent that can experience the pain of manual QA testing for you
cooking.summary: Momentic is building agents that navigate your app to catch bugs, effectively automating the most tedious part of a software release. It's like having an intern who actually enjoys clicking every single button on your site for eight hours straight.
cooking.plain_english: Momentic has developed automated software agents that test applications for bugs by interacting with them just like a human user would.

cooking.headline: BYD is speedrunning the EV market while the US is still buffering
cooking.summary: BYD sold more electric vehicles in a single month than the entire United States managed to move in a full quarter. It turns out that when you actually build the cars people want to buy, the sales numbers tend to do the heavy lifting for you.
cooking.plain_english: The Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer BYD sold more cars in one month than all electric vehicle manufacturers combined sold in the United States over three months.

cooked.headline: China just added a 'Terms and Conditions' page to AI exports
cooked.summary: China is officially putting export controls on frontier AI models, making the international tech trade feel like a complicated school project with too many permission slips. It's hard to build a global product when your model needs a travel visa just to cross a border.
cooked.plain_english: The Chinese government has introduced new regulations that require official approval before certain advanced artificial intelligence models can be exported to other countries.

cooked.headline: Ubuntu is treating a critical RCE like a group project deadline
cooked.summary: It has been three weeks since a critical remote code execution vulnerability was identified, yet Ubuntu still hasn't shipped the patch. It's like waiting for that one teammate to finally upload their slides five minutes before the presentation starts.
cooked.plain_english: Ubuntu has not yet released a security update for a major software vulnerability that was discovered three weeks ago.

cooked.headline: Trigger.dev just accidentally shared their secret sauce with the world
cooked.summary: Trigger.dev managed to expose their customer environment variables, effectively turning their entire security strategy into a public API. It turns out that keeping your secrets secret is significantly harder than building a tool that automates everything else.
cooked.plain_english: Trigger.dev experienced a security incident where sensitive environment configuration settings belonging to their customers were exposed.

cooked.headline: Your frozen pizza is now part of a botnet
cooked.summary: Europe's supermarket freezers are getting hacked, proving that even your dinner is now a potential attack vector. We really spent decades putting computers in everything just to have our ice cream held for ransom.
cooked.plain_english: A series of cyber-attacks has disrupted the operation of commercial freezer systems across Europe.
